newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Pollution remains high in Russia, official says.
newsitem.headline: Pollution remains high in Russia, official says.

text.p: Pollution remains "unacceptably high" in Russia, with 40 percent of people living in cities where air pollution exceeds admissable levels, the country's top environment official said on Wednesday.

Viktor Danilov-Danilyan, head of the state committee for the environment, was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying air pollution was inadmissably high in more than 200 cities and towns with a combined population of more than 60 million.
Of these cities, 120 had pollution levels five times higher than the permitted maximum, Tass said.
Danilov-Danilyan, citing figures for the end of 1996 at a meeting of his committee, said about 40 percent of the total volume of dumped waste water in Russia was polluted.
He said pollution of surface water had grown and most polluted water was located in the European part of Russia.
Tass quoted him as saying Russia was losing from 150,000 to 180,000 hectares of woodland each year -- one-third of it because of forest fires.
The number of wildlife species had also fallen because of an increase in poaching, Tass said, but gave no details.
Many of Russia's pollution problems date back to Soviet times, when the communist authorities paid little attention to environmental issues.
A rising number of cars in major cities and lax emission controls -- unleaded petrol is rarely available -- have contributed to worsening air pollution.
